text:
taylor: Heads-up — noticed a new P99 latency regression on multi-GPU inference after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. Spike looks correlated with all-reduce stall time when KV prefetch is on, ~2.3x increase in tail.

raj: Can you paste the trace? Is this on dedicated or private? Which model / batch shape?

taylor: Dedicated cluster (rp-dedicated-3), model: redwood-large-v1, sequence ~1024, batch 8. nsys capture uploaded: https://perf.internal/trace/191760. Summary from perf-bot below.

perf-bot: Profiling summary: allreduce_wait_time +55% vs baseline, cudaGraphCapture=enabled for that run, cross-stream submissions observed, KV-prefetch latency increased. See /reports/191760.

emily: If capture spans kernels that are launched on different streams (prefetch stream vs compute stream) the graph capture can effectively serialize them — we flattened ordering in a past incident. Could be a change in kernel selection moved some ops to default stream or changed async memcpy behavior.

josh: I repro locally with a mini-repro. Quick snippet: 
```
cudaStream_t s0, s1;
cudaStreamCreate(&s0);
cudaStreamCreate(&s1);
// kv prefetch enqueues on s1
kv_cache.prefetch(keys, s1);
// begin capture on s0
cudaGraphBegin(s0);
launch_forward(s0);
cudaGraphEnd();
```
When capture is active the prefetch ends up serialized before the all-reduce because capture captured cross-stream sequence. If I disable cudaGraph capture in the runtime the p99 goes back to baseline.

raj: Which change touched kernels? Wasn't there a kernel-selector PR that preferred a fused kernel last week?

emily: Yes PR #5123 changed kernel preference to the new "fast-fused" kernel for several transformer blocks. That kernel also performs a small host->device memcpy for quantized dequant path in a way that ends up on the default stream (we missed an explicit stream affinity). Combined with earlier batching heuristic changes that prefetch earlier, we now have a cross-stream capture surface.

josh: nsys flame: timeline shows allreduce start blocked until prefetch on s1 completes because capture serialized the submission ordering. The blocking period equals the prefetch memcpy + kvcache lookup (~10-20ms depending on keys). That's the p99 hit.

taylor: Quick mitigations: (A) revert kernel-selector fallback for "fast-fused" (risky perf revert), (B) guard KV prefetch to skip if cudaGraphCaptureActive(), (C) enforce captured streams include prefetch stream (harder). Thoughts?

raj: (B) seems safest and fastest. Skip prefetch when capture active so we avoid cross-stream enqueues during capture. Open a canary with that; monitor p99. If that doesn't fix, we roll back the kernel change.

emily: Also add a unit/integration test that runs a short capture and ensures no cross-stream prefetch enqueues during capture. Add docs to Optimize about "capture-sensitive" heuristics.

perf-bot: Created perf-gate ticket RL-4321: "skip-kv-prefetch-during-graph-capture" and queued canary to rp-dedicated-3.

josh: I'll validate with nsight capture after canary finishes. If p99 back to baseline I'll promote. If not, we'll revert PR #5123.

taylor: Filed follow-ups RL-4322 (repro harness + unit test) and RL-4323 (postmortem). Thanks team. :thumbsup:

raj: Small action item: add a runtime assert log when cudaGraphCaptureActive() is true and we attempt cross-stream prefetch, so future regressions are noisy.

emily: Agreed. Also note for the release notes: "capture interaction with kernel stream affinity" under known issues until PR fixes land.

perf-bot: Canary job completed (canary-191760-1): p99 reduced to baseline (-1.1% change). Marking RL-4321 as in-review.

taylor: Great — closing the loop. We'll keep the kernel-selector change behind a feature flag until we add explicit stream affinity in the fused kernel."
